tools.name: remotelock_get_account
tools.description: The RemoteLock account these credentials belong to: name, plan limits and settings. Use it to confirm which account is connected. GET /account.

tools.name: remotelock_list_locations
tools.description: List the account's locations (properties/sites) with address and time zone. Use the ids to filter devices. GET /locations.

tools.name: remotelock_get_location
tools.description: One location by id. GET /locations/{id}.

tools.name: remotelock_list_devices
tools.description: List devices: locks, access-control doors, thermostats, etc., with name, model, battery/connectivity state, lock state and location. Filter by type (e.g. lock) or location. GET /devices.

tools.name: remotelock_get_device
tools.description: One device (lock) by id with its full state: connectivity, battery/power, lock state, auto-lock settings, model and location. GET /devices/{id}.

tools.name: remotelock_lock_device
tools.description: WRITE: sends the lock command to a lock (it locks the door). Locking an already locked door changes nothing. PUT /devices/{id}/lock.

tools.name: remotelock_unlock_device
tools.description: WRITE, SECURITY-SENSITIVE: sends the unlock command to a lock, which physically unlocks the door. Only call it when the user explicitly asked to unlock this specific door, and set confirm to true. PUT /devices/{id}/unlock.

tools.name: remotelock_list_access_persons
tools.description: List the people who can open doors: access users (permanent) and access guests (time-limited), with name, email, status, validity window and their PIN / card number. By default only current and upcoming people; pass status to include expired or deactivated. GET /access_persons.

tools.name: remotelock_get_access_person
tools.description: One access user or guest by id, with status, validity window and PIN / card number. GET /access_persons/{id}.

tools.name: remotelock_create_access_user
tools.description: WRITE: creates a permanent access user (an employee, resident or owner) with a PIN and/or card. It creates the person only; use remotelock_grant_access to give them doors. The reply includes the PIN. Check remotelock_list_access_persons first to avoid duplicates. POST /access_persons.

tools.name: remotelock_create_access_guest
tools.description: WRITE: creates an access guest whose PIN/card only works between starts_at and ends_at (local time of the lock). It creates the person only; use remotelock_grant_access to give them doors. The reply includes the PIN. POST /access_persons.

tools.name: remotelock_deactivate_access_person
tools.description: WRITE: deactivates an access user or guest, so their PIN/card stops working on every door. The person stays in the account (status deactivated) and is not deleted. Only do it when the user asked. PUT /access_persons/{id}/deactivate.

tools.name: remotelock_list_person_accesses
tools.description: List the doors, door groups and locations one access user or guest can open, with sync state per device. GET /access_persons/{id}/accesses.

tools.name: remotelock_list_device_accesses
tools.description: List the access users and guests who have access to one lock (and whether the PIN is synced to it). GET /devices/{id}/access_person_accesses.

tools.name: remotelock_grant_access
tools.description: WRITE: gives an access user or guest access to a lock, a door group or a location, so their PIN/card opens it. RemoteLock then syncs the code to the lock(s). Optionally limit the hours with an access schedule (access_schedule_id, for recurring daily hours) or override a guest's start/end time of day

tools.name: remotelock_revoke_access
tools.description: WRITE: removes one access grant (an id from remotelock_list_person_accesses), so the person's PIN/card no longer opens that door, door group or location. The person itself stays. Only do it when the user asked. DELETE /access_persons/{id}/accesses/{access_id}.

tools.name: remotelock_list_door_groups
tools.description: List door groups (named sets of locks you can grant access to in one step). GET /groups.

tools.name: remotelock_list_group_items
tools.description: List the items (locks) that belong to one door group. GET /groups/{id}/items.

tools.name: remotelock_list_notifications
tools.description: List notifications sent by notification subscriptions: each names the lock (publisher), the event type (unlocked, access_denied, jammed, power_level_low, ...) and an event_id. Only events that match a subscription appear. Get details with remotelock_get_event. GET /notifications.

tools.name: remotelock_get_event
tools.description: One event by id (for example from a notification): type, time, source, status, the lock and the person involved, and the method used. The PIN or card used is not returned. GET /events/{id}.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "remotelock_get_account" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: The RemoteLock account these credentials belong to: name, plan limits and settings. Use it to confirm which account is connected. GET /account.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: remotelock_list_access_persons, remotelock_create_access_user, remotelock_list_notifications, remotelock_get_event · Private data: remotelock_get_account · Public sink: remotelock_list_access_persons, remotelock_create_access_user, remotelock_create_access_guest, remotelock_grant_access · Destructive: remotelock_revoke_access.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: remotelock_list_access_persons, remotelock_create_access_user, remotelock_list_notifications, remotelock_get_event · Private data: remotelock_get_account · Public sink: remotelock_list_access_persons, remotelock_create_access_user, remotelock_create_access_guest, remotelock_grant_access · Destructive: remotelock_revoke_access

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
